audit.whatIsWrong: Five of the seven chart rows disagreed with their own whys. Rows 2, 3 and 5 said Urgot while whys[2] ('coin-flip skill fight'), whys[3] ('keeps the lane even') and whys[5] ('evening the fight') say even; row 0 said Skill while whys[0] says your Q poke out-damages him; row 6 said Skill while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Wukong outscales you.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Urgot, Urgot, Skill, Skill, Urgot, Skill, Wukong — identical to what the whys already describe. At 51.5% over 1429 games this is a near-even lane, not a stomp.
audit.corrected: All five rows flipped in both layers with matching ratings, and the four full-layer whys rewritten so they stop claiming an Urgot win.
sources: content whys[0], whys[2], whys[3], whys[5], whys[6]

audit.why: Spike placement is right: Urgot early and at level 5, Wukong at level 6 Cyclone and at his first bruiser item, with the late game his. phases[5].why now names the Cyclone spike instead of describing a first-item Urgot spike that the chart no longer claims.
audit.corrected: Spike text left alone; phases[5].why realigned to the level-6/first-item Wukong swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow's auto-attack reset is never mentioned anywhere, so the page never tells the player what the commit tell actually is. dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d were generic filler under titles about the decoy and about being dived.
audit.why: The missing-interactions file flags Crushing Blow as an auto-attack reset: the wind-up animation, not the ability cast, is the moment to step back. And Urgot's E is a 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s cooldown — holding a shoved wave without it is what makes the dive free.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now states the Crushing Blow reset tell; dontsFull[1].d carries the 16s rank-1 E cooldown and the wave rule.

edits.before: Full legs rotation online — this is your lane now. Walk Wukong down with W whenever Nimbus Strike is on cooldown.
edits.after: Full legs rotation online, but Warrior Trickster answers it — bait the decoy with a W-lock before you spend the real one.

edits.before: Q and W ranks make the grind trades brutal. Force Wukong to choose between CS and health; he can't have both into your spray.
edits.after: Q and W ranks make the grind trades brutal, but the decoy-and-vanish pattern keeps him alive through them — the lane stays even.

edits.before: Black Cleaver stacks instantly with W — your shred turns even tanky answers soft. Shove and force Wukong to trade into the spike.
edits.after: Black Cleaver stacks instantly with W, but Cyclone gives him a knock-up all-in at 6 — hold E for his engage, not for the wave.

edits.before: Sterak's + Cleaver makes your W-trades unloseable head-on. Wukong must dodge E forever or find a jungler — punish the first mistake with R.
edits.after: Two items in he outscales you: Cyclone is a fight-ending engage and the clone makes your execute unreliable — group and stop duelling him.

edits.before: Wukong wastes Nimbus Strike — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Crushing Blow resets his auto — the wind-up is your cue, not the cast.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Your E is down 16s at rank 1 — never hold a shoved wave without it up.

notes: enemyKit was null in this brief — Wukong's kit data did not come through, so I had no cooldowns, ranges or Riot descriptions for him. Every edit here is therefore driven by the packet's ability names, the missing-interactions entry, Urgot's own kit numbers, and the internal contradiction between chart and whys. Two existing claims I could NOT verify and deliberately left untouched: (1) the page calls Stone Skin an 'armor-shred passive' in spikes[2].text, spikes[3].text, late and wants.foe[1] — Stone Skin reads as a defensive passive by name and armour-shred sounds wrong, but with no kit I will not assert it; (2) spikes[1].text and whys[5] say Cyclone is 'a knock-up spin he can flash into' — Flash-buffering is explicitly not in Riot's text, so I avoided repeating it in my own rewrite of phases[5].why.
